subject: Post-demo: deployment tradeoffs and dedicated sizing next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Liza Chen <liza.chen@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: deployment tradeoffs and dedicated sizing next steps

Thanks for taking the demo today, Liza — appreciate the time. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Key constraints we heard from your side:
   - Low-latency inference for customer-facing personalization (95th pctl goal: ~120ms)
   - High average tokens per request (avg ~1,200; peak up to ~4,500)
   - Strict data residency: primary US region, eventual on-prem options for PCI-sensitive workloads

2) Deployment tradeoffs we discussed:
   - Hosted API: fastest to ship but harder to guarantee latency SLO at peak without dedicated capacity
   - Dedicated capacity: predictable throughput, GPU pooling; good fit if you want the 95th pctl latency and predictable cost profile
   - Private (VPC/on-prem): recommended for the PCI-scoped flows, requires network design work and separate SLA discussions

3) Immediate asks from Redwood to size a Dedicated starting point (see attached workbook):
   - Target sustained TPS: 18 reqs/sec (you mentioned burst to ~45 reqs/sec)
   - Token distribution: 70% short (<=512 tokens), 20% medium (512-2,048), 10% long (>2,048)
   - Preferred GPU family: you indicated a willingness to test both A100 and H100 variants for latency vs cost tradeoffs

Next steps (proposed):
- ACME: confirm burst window length (how long do you see sustained 45 TPS? Typical burst profile?)
- ACME: share expected QPS per customer cohort (if available) so we can estimate prefix caching impact
- Redwood: we will return a 2-scenario Dedicated sizing workbook (conservative / optimized) and a short checklist for Private onboarding network requirements by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx (spreadsheet)

— Diego
Diego Fernandez | Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Liza Chen <liza.chen@acme-retail.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 17:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment tradeoffs and dedicated sizing next steps

Thanks, Diego — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Burst behavior: bursts are typically short (30–90s) around peak shopping hours, but during promotions we can see sustained higher TPS for ~10–20 minutes.
- Token mix: the numbers you used look right for our personalization API, but for the search/QA endpoint token counts skew longer (we estimate ~30% >2,048 for QA). We'll attach a sample token-profile CSV by tomorrow.
- GPU family: we prefer to start with H100 for the QA/high-token paths and try an A100-backed pool for short-chat paths if that makes sense operationally.

On procurement: our procurement team will need SOC 2 summary and an initial SSO/SCIM integration plan to start the security review. Putting procurement on CC (procurement@acme-retail.com).

Liza
Liza Chen | Head of ML Platform | Acme Retail

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Liza Chen <liza.chen@acme-retail.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment tradeoffs and dedicated sizing next steps

Appreciate the details, Liza. Quick notes from our sizing playbook perspective: 
- We'll model two pools in the workbook: 
   * H100-heavy pool sized for the QA endpoint (assumes 30% requests are long-token, with KV caching less effective for QA)
   * A100-mixed pool for short/medium workloads with aggressive prefix caching and batching enabled
- For bursts of ~45 TPS for up to 20 minutes, autoscaling + burst capacity is the right approach; we'll show both a steady-state committed baseline and a burst buffer in the workbook.
- I'll add a short appendix on how quantization choices change the GPU footprint and expected latency for long-token requests.

Marissa

From: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Liza Chen <liza.chen@acme-retail.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Request: SOC 2 summary + SSO integration plan for vendor review

Team,

Please share the SOC 2 summary and a short SSO/SCIM integration plan so we can open a security intake. Also include estimated timelines for Private (VPC) onboarding versus Dedicated capacity provisioning. We prefer a one-page RACI for network changes required for VPC.

Thanks,
Procurement — Acme Retail
(attachment requested: soc2-summary.pdf)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-retail.com>, Liza Chen <liza.chen@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 summary + SSO integration plan for vendor review

Hi Procurement team — attaching the SOC 2 summary and a short SSO/SCIM checklist (stubs included below). We can also spin up a 1-hour security walkthrough next week with our security engineering lead if that helps accelerate the intake. 

Attachments included: soc2-summary.pdf (summary), redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx (workbook), acme-network-diagram.png (customer-provided)

SSO/SCIM checklist (high level):
- SCIM: Redwood supports SCIM v2 for group + user sync. We will provide a connector URL and temporary client credentials for initial sync.
- SAML SSO: Metadata XML and ACS endpoints provided; we support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows.
- Onboarding timeline estimate: Dedicated capacity baseline provisioning (if committed): 2–3 weeks; Private VPC onboarding (network + audit): 4–6 weeks depending on firewall and cross-account routing work.

Next steps: we will finalize the two-scenario workbook (conservative vs optimized) and a short network RACI by EOD Friday.

— Diego
